corrected_smoke_attempts: The first detection smoke reached actual root finding delivery, then DeleteBucket returned BucketNotEmpty. The owned CloudTrail bucket is now emptied before deletion.

The temporary-root smoke initially expected IAM success from non-MFA GetSessionToken credentials. IAM correctly returned AccessDenied; the smoke now verifies that denial is retained in a separate short-term root finding.
The first S3 Control smoke attempted account-prefixed IP hostname resolution. The local client now uses EndpointResolverV2 with the actual IP listener and signed account header.

The password-policy smoke initially expected a separate finding for a missing-policy delete. Retained SQLite evidence showed count 2 and latest NoSuchEntityException in the same aggregate. The smoke now verifies stable finding identity and latest recorded audit outcome.

The first retention smoke passed its API assertions but stopped the original controller before deferred EventBridge cleanup. The controller now stays alive until that cleanup completes; the full corrected run exited successfully.

The IP-list workflow initially expected immediate service-linked-role deletion after detector deletion. Actual ingestion had issued live role sessions. The smoke now verifies IAM's active-session rejection, advances manual service time one hour, and verifies successful deletion without changing IAM enforcement.

The throwaway detection harness initially bypassed net/http transport normalization and supplied an incorrect feature enum. It was corrected to an actual local HTTP server and the modeled AI_ANALYST enum before the successful detection/KMS run.
The destination smoke initially rejected the native continuation on a full final page. It now follows the cursor through the terminal empty page.

The destination smoke initially used root to enable detection, which legitimately generated an additional UpdateDetector root finding. A named IAM controller now isolates the intentional root ListKeys source without suppressing detection.

After implementing EKS audit protection, the S3 rollback smoke no longer assumes that EKS_AUDIT_LOGS activation fails. It now rejects the documented mutually exclusive EKS_RUNTIME_MONITORING/RUNTIME_MONITORING pair and verifies that enabled S3 protection was not partially disabled.
limits: Samples and actual observed API findings are separate. Implemented structured rules do not reproduce AWS private anomaly scoring or grouping.

Public-access-block rules identify successful disabling requests, not proven public exposure or prior true-to-false transitions. Exact native partial-setting detection eligibility and grouping remain uncalibrated.

Public bucket grant rules consume admitted ACL groups and bounded unconditional or literal SecureTransport/PrincipalAccount/PrincipalIsAWSService-conditioned anonymous bucket-policy proofs, not IsPublic or effective access after Block Public Access. Other condition/variable-resource proofs, additional unsigned operations, authenticated policy audiences and native event eligibility/grouping remain open; no Zelkova-equivalence claim.
Password-policy detection implements documented update/delete attempts, not inferred policy weakening. Aggregation retains the latest outcome; the source journal retains individual API events.

Enabled S3 data events feed the implemented authenticated root-use and CloudTrail log-deletion predicates only, not all S3 finding types or private anomaly models. DNS and flow telemetry consumers remain absent.

Retention uses a conservative creation-based 90-day cap. AWS documents the maximum retention period but not whether aggregation resets its timestamp anchor; native refreshed-finding expiry remains uncalibrated.
The 444 native sample variants and 102-operation inventory do not establish behavioral completeness.

Legacy list lifecycle and source-error calibration do not establish native custom-threat timing/grouping or service-owned policy naming/granularity. New entity lists and member propagation remain unimplemented.

S3 exports use local deterministic five-minute initial/retry deadlines and one finding per gzip JSONL object. Native export eligibility, exact payload/batching, naming and retry timing remain uncalibrated despite the bounded native captures. Explicit-prefix caller denial and its GuardDuty error envelope are calibrated separately.
Native disabled and enabled-core event probes received no finding event within their 300-second windows; native event eligibility, latency and full payload equivalence remain uncalibrated.
Native exact-owned service-linked role cleanup remains unresolved after terminal AWS internal-error deletion failures; local cleanup passed.
No repository-wide test or race checkpoint was run.
